title: Sanctioned opposition rally in Oral (Uralsk)
organizer: Local organizer not specified; RFE/RL attributes the broader multi-city call to the Democratic Party and DVK.
participants_original: RFE/RL describes several hundred; Tirek estimates about 300.
threshold_50_evidence: The reported Oral estimates are several hundred (RFE/RL) and about 300 (Tirek), both above 50; neither supports exact numerical bounds.

start_date.summary: Both reports describe an opposition rally in Oral on February 28.

location.summary: Oral is the reported city; it is also commonly rendered Uralsk.

scope.summary: The Oral action is a single city gathering within reporting of other separate city actions.

organizer.summary: RFE/RL attributes the wider calls to the Democratic Party and DVK; the local Oral organizer is not separately identified.

demands.summary: Tirek reports demands to release political prisoners and oppose land sales to foreigners; RFE/RL describes political-reform and activist-persecution demands.

participants_original.summary: RFE/RL says several hundred; Tirek says about 300.

participants_min.summary: No exact lower bound is reported.

participants_max.summary: No exact upper bound is reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both Oral estimates clearly exceed 50 but are approximate.

end_date.summary: Neither read report establishes when this gathering physically ended.

protester_violence.summary: No Oral-specific account in the reviewed text establishes protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: RFE/RL says the sanctioned Oral rally had no detentions. Other response variables are unknown; sanctioning alone is not coded as accommodation.

notes: The political and land-policy demands are attributed to the Oral gathering in the reviewed reporting. Other cities are separate actions; do not pool their attendance or detentions. No continuity beyond this date is established.
open_questions: Exact turnout and physical end time.
Local organizer identity and whether the city-specific demands were identical to the national call.
Independent source-lineage review and official baseline reconciliation.

title: Nur-Sultan crane operators’ labor campaign
location: Nur-Sultan; Zheruyik Park gatherings reported on February 19 and 26
organizer: Crane operators; named organization not reported.
threshold_50_evidence: The retrospective report gives no attendance count for the campaign or its park gatherings; threshold is unresolved.

start_date.summary: The retrospective report says the crane operators’ protest campaign began February 12; its publication date is not used as the event date.

location.summary: The report locates meetings after work at Zheruyik Park on February 19 and 26; it does not locate the February 12 action more precisely.

scope.summary: The described action concerns crane operators in Nur-Sultan.

organizer.summary: Workers are identified as crane operators; no named organizer is supplied.

demands.summary: Reported demands include higher wages, contracts/social payments, safer conditions, shorter working hours and lower retirement ages; coded under the available labor-dispute category.

participants_original.summary: The report does not give attendance.

participants_min.summary: No published lower bound for attendance.

participants_max.summary: No published upper bound for attendance.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd estimate is given for the reported meetings.

end_date.summary: Two meeting dates are stated, but the campaign’s physical end is not.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed article does not establish protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: A state labor inspector met workers February 28 and promised a conditional labor-rights check. The source does not establish completed inspection or a concession; coded response variables remain unknown.

notes: The report is retrospective and describes a campaign beginning February 12, with meetings documented on February 19 and 26. Do not infer continuous occupation between them. A letter to the labor ministry and inspector meeting are reported; the campaign’s end and the check outcome are unknown.
open_questions: Attendance at each public meeting and whether the February 12 start was itself a public gathering.
Whether there were intervening actions or a continuous episode.
Whether the promised labor inspection occurred and whether any state accommodation followed.

title: Shymkent Bus drivers’ work stoppage over pay and terms
location: Shymkent; specific gathering site not reported
organizer: Shymkent Bus drivers and conductors; named organizer not reported.
participants_original: The headline characterizes the number as roughly 500; the article body gives a company workforce of 550 drivers but does not count participants.
threshold_50_evidence: Turnout is not established: headline, workforce and route figures are not an attendee count, and no public-gathering size is supplied.

start_date.summary: The report says the work stoppage began at 05:00 on February 3.

location.summary: The report locates the work stoppage in Shymkent but gives no specific gathering site.

scope.summary: The described labor action concerns the city bus company.

organizer.summary: Drivers and conductors are described as stopping work; no named organizer is reported.

demands.summary: The article reports complaints about pay and work terms.

participants_original.summary: The headline characterizes the number as roughly 500; the article body gives a company workforce of 550 drivers but does not count participants.

participants_min.summary: No turnout lower bound is reported.

participants_max.summary: No turnout upper bound is reported; fleet workforce and routes are not attendee bounds.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Fourteen of twenty routes were not staffed for several hours, but route counts and the company workforce do not establish the number who took part or gathered publicly.

end_date.summary: The article says the work stoppage lasted several hours, with no physical end clock.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed text does not establish protester violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: The source reports city officials visited and promised a pay increase. This is coded as an official accommodation statement only; implementation is not established. Other response variables are unknown.

notes: A work stoppage is reported, but the source does not establish a public gathering or its attendance. Workers primarily sought pay/work-term changes from their employer; municipal involvement is reported, so state-target status remains for review. A promised pay increase is not proof of implementation.
open_questions: Whether a public gathering of at least 50 occurred, and the number of participants.
Whether the grievances included an explicit demand on the Kazakhstan state or public policy rather than the employer alone.
Whether promised pay changes were implemented.
